    <div class="content-card">
        <h2>How to Get to Cardiff</h2>

        <h3>By Air</h3>

        <h4>Heathrow / Gatwick Airports</h4>
        <p>National Express coaches and rail services operate direct connections to Cardiff Central Station from London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports.</p>
        <p><strong>Useful links:</strong> <a href="https://www.traveline-cymru.org.uk" target="_blank">Rail service information</a> | <a href="https://www.nationalexpress.com" target="_blank">National Express</a></p>

        <h4>Bristol Airport</h4>
        <p>Bristol Airport is 50 miles (80 km) from Cardiff. Journey time is approximately two hours.</p>
        <p><strong>By Coach:</strong> The Greyhound UK coach service runs every two hours from Bristol Airport to Cardiff Bus Station. Single fare: GBP 6. Tickets can be bought online at <a href="https://www.greyhounduk.com/" target="_blank">www.greyhounduk.com</a>.</p>
        <p><strong>By Train:</strong> Take the Bristol International Flyer from the airport to Bristol Temple Meads train station (GBP 7). From Bristol Temple Meads, trains to Cardiff Central run every 30 minutes. One-way tickets are approximately GBP 10.</p>
        <p><strong>Alternative:</strong> Take the Bristol International Flyer bus to Bristol city centre or Bristol Bus Station, then catch a National Express coach to Cardiff. One-way fares are typically around GBP 10.</p>

        <h4>Cardiff International Airport</h4>
        <p>The airport is 11 miles from the city centre. Visit <a href="https://www.cwlfly.com" target="_blank">www.cwlfly.com</a> for more information.</p>

        <h3>By Rail</h3>
        <p>High-speed intercity trains provide frequent services between Cardiff and major British cities. The Cardiff to London Paddington service runs throughout the day, with a journey time of under two hours.</p>
        <p><strong>Frequent regional services connect Cardiff with:</strong></p>
        <ul>
            <li>Bristol (50 mins)</li>
            <li>Birmingham (2 hrs 10 mins)</li>
            <li>Southampton (2 hrs 30 mins)</li>
            <li>Manchester (3 hrs)</li>
            <li>Liverpool (3 hrs)</li>
        </ul>
        <p><strong>Rail enquiries:</strong> 0870 6082608 | <a href="https://www.nationalrail.co.uk" target="_blank">www.nationalrail.co.uk</a></p>

        <h3>By Road</h3>
        <p>Cardiff is served by the M4 and is easily accessible from all parts of Britain.</p>
        <p><strong>From the southwest:</strong> Take the M5.<br>
        <strong>From the south of England:</strong> Follow major A roads to the M4.<br>
        <strong>From Scotland, northern England, and the Midlands:</strong> Travel via the M50 to the M4.</p>
        <p><strong>Travelling east on the M4:</strong> Leave at Junction 32 and follow the A470, signposted City Centre, into the Cathays area of the city.</p>
        <p><strong>Travelling west on the M4:</strong> Leave at Junction 29 and follow the A48(M)/A48, signposted Cardiff East and South, to the A470. Continue on the A470 towards the city centre.</p>

        <h4>Car Parking</h4>
        <p>There are several short- and long-stay public car parks in the city centre. Cardiff is compact and easy to explore on foot, with most attractions, shops, restaurants, hotels, and green spaces within a short walk. Cardiff Bay is around 1 km from the city centre and can be reached on foot, by cycle path, or by bus.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="content-card">
        <h2>Things to Do in Cardiff</h2>
        <p>Cardiff is a vibrant capital city that combines historic landmarks with modern architecture, strong cultural institutions, and a lively food and shopping scene.</p>
        <p>For full details, visit the official Cardiff visitor website: <a href="https://www.visitcardiff.com" target="_blank">www.visitcardiff.com</a>.</p>

        <h3>City Centre</h3>
        <p>Many attractions are located in the city centre, including <strong>Cardiff Castle</strong>, the <strong>National Museum</strong>, and the <strong>Principality Stadium</strong>. Parks, hotels, shopping centres, and Victorian arcades are all within a short walk.</p>

        <h3>Dining & Shopping</h3>
        <p>The <strong>Brewery Quarter</strong> and <strong>Mill Lane</strong> offer a wide range of restaurants and bars. Nearby, <strong>Queen Street</strong> and <strong>St David's</strong> provide a mix of major retailers, designer brands, and independent shops, while the city's arcades retain their Victorian and Edwardian character.</p>

        <h3>Cardiff Bay</h3>
        <p><strong>Mermaid Quay</strong> in Cardiff Bay offers restaurants, cafes, and waterside activities around a large freshwater lake. The area also includes the <strong>Senedd</strong> and the <strong>Wales Millennium Centre</strong>.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="content-card">
        <h2>Exploring Wales</h2>
        <p>Beyond Cardiff, Wales offers coastlines, mountain landscapes, market towns, and historic castles that are easy to reach during a longer stay.</p>
        <p>Explore <strong>Snowdonia National Park</strong>, the beaches and coastal paths of <strong>Pembrokeshire</strong>, or the hiking routes and dark skies of the <strong>Brecon Beacons</strong>. Towns such as <strong>Hay-on-Wye</strong> and <strong>Tenby</strong>, along with sites such as <strong>Caerphilly Castle</strong> and <strong>Conwy Castle</strong>, offer a wider sense of Wales beyond the city.</p>
    </div>
